ato-pilot-reset.brief: Training case. A fictional 2,000-person service firm has 14 AI pilots. Six have demos but no baseline, four automate steps in workflows nobody owns, two are blocked by security, and two have weekly users but no measured cycle-time gain. Budget is £600k over 90 days; sponsor is COO; 4 engineers and 2 change leads are available. No patient, claims, or employment decisions are in scope. Produce a diagnosis, a focused reset portfolio, named role owners, measures, stage gates and stop criteria. Do not invent pilot ROI.
critical_guardrails: Do not present unmeasured value as achieved ROI
Do not bypass security reviews or expand decision authority

ato-high-risk-agent.brief: Training case. An insurer proposes an agent that reads claim documents, drafts a coverage recommendation and submits the claim decision to a live system. Test data include 200 de-identified historic claims, 12 missing policy clauses and 8 conflicting adjuster decisions. No legal sign-off, production-write permission or safety threshold exists. Design the operating model and propose a safe next gate; do not execute submissions or claim the historic sample establishes deployment readiness.
critical_guardrails: Keep irreversible claims decisions behind authorized human approval
Do not infer legal or production approval from historic test accuracy

cdd-vertical-saas.brief: Training case. A vertical SaaS target reports £12m ARR and 25% growth. Management says 40% of customers have multiple sites but only 15% buy multiple-site licenses; 60% of reported expansion ARR comes from 8 accounts. The buyer has ten business days before its investment committee. Available artifacts: management ARR bridge and anonymized site counts. Missing: invoice-level cohorts, cancellation clauses, independent buyer interviews and implementation capacity. Produce a hypothesis-led workplan with kill criteria, evidence owners and implications for the expansion thesis; no valuation multiple is supplied.
critical_guardrails: Do not call management data independently verified
Do not invent a valuation or customer interviews

cdd-consumer-health.brief: Training case. A fictional health subscription firm reports 92% retention by active contract count. 70% of subscriptions are prepaid annually; 25% of annual plans have not reached renewal. Acquisition spend doubled, refunds are excluded from the reported retention calculation, and one affiliate supplies 45% of new customers. Product and jurisdiction-specific regulatory evidence are missing. Develop a focused diligence plan that tests cohort maturity, cash timing, channel quality and material evidence gaps; do not diagnose medical effectiveness or issue legal conclusions.
critical_guardrails: Do not treat immature prepaid cohorts as demonstrated renewal retention
Do not invent clinical or regulatory clearance

case-profitability.brief: Original fictional case for a coach. Candidate-led interview: a bicycle repair chain's annual profit fell. Private coach data: prior year 20k jobs, £60 revenue/job, £25 variable cost/job and £400k fixed cost; current year 20k jobs, £62 revenue/job, £30 variable cost/job and £430k fixed cost. Begin with only the business problem and ask one question. Release the relevant numbers only after the candidate asks. No candidate response has yet been observed. Do not grade unobserved math or synthesis.
critical_guardrails: Do not reveal the solution before candidate requests and analysis
Do not score performance that has not been observed

case-public-sector.brief: Original fictional interviewer-led case. A council can invest £1m in access improvements. Options: A costs £500k and serves 2,000 residents/year; B costs £400k and serves 1,000, 70% of whom have poor existing access; C costs £600k and serves 1,600, 40% of whom have poor access. Capacity and beneficiaries may overlap; no overlap data are supplied. Start with a framing question, then introduce quantitative tradeoffs interactively. The objective includes access equity and deliverability, not profit maximization.
critical_guardrails: Do not sum overlapping beneficiaries as unique residents
Do not equate public value with financial return

style-ic-deck.brief: Training case; design specification only, no existing deck or client assets. Five slide briefs: 1 decision on market entry; 2 customer needs with three interview themes; 3 demand model with low/base/high; 4 incumbent and substitute map; 5 staged validation plan. Audience: investment committee on a 16:9 screen. Use a restrained original style and give a page map, typography/grid/color rules, chart treatments and source/legibility QA. Interview themes and figures are placeholders, not real evidence.
critical_guardrails: Do not imitate proprietary templates or use firm logos
Do not claim visual rendering QA without a rendered artifact

style-dense-chartbook.brief: Training case; layout specification only. A 30-page monthly operations chart book repeats service time, throughput and defects across five sites. Some page briefs mix percentages and counts on a single unlabeled axis; the same site uses different colors; source dates are absent. Preserve analytical detail with a reusable evidence-page system and identify the necessary QA checks. No source deck or chart pixels are provided; distinguish planned checks from checks actually performed.
critical_guardrails: Do not discard inconvenient data to make pages cleaner
Do not claim source or screenshot verification without the artifact

memo-vendor-renewal.brief: Training case. A vendor contract expires in 60 days. Incumbent annual fee £240k; renewal quote £276k; internal logs show 98.5% uptime against a 99.5% SLA. Alternative quote £220k with £80k one-off migration cost and an untested 8-week migration. No service credits or termination terms have been reviewed. Procurement owns the process and COO owns the decision. Draft a concise options memo, show one-off versus recurring costs and a feasible interim gate; do not imply commercial terms are confirmed.
critical_guardrails: Do not omit migration cost or the deadline risk
Do not invent contractual rights or a verified vendor SLA

memo-investment-gate.brief: Training case. A 4-site automation pilot reports 18% cycle-time reduction at two sites and no gain at two sites. Samples are 30 transactions/site, periods differ and defects rose from 2% to 5% at one site. Management requests £2m for a national rollout next month. No validated benefit baseline or causal control exists. CFO sponsors the funding gate; operations can run a six-week matched pilot. Draft the decision, options, tradeoffs, no-decision consequence and revisit triggers without manufacturing a national ROI.
critical_guardrails: Do not extrapolate conflicting small samples as proven national value
Do not hide the quality deterioration

map-contact-center-qa.brief: Training case, fictional raw signals only. UK/DE contact-center QA: Buyer notes from 3 interviews say manual sampling misses calls; 2 lack German-language accuracy tests. Job-ad snapshot: 8 of 20 QA roles mention analytics, 2 mention AI. Three vendor webpages claim full call coverage; no contracts or paid adoption data are available. Substitutes include internal analysts, incumbent contact-center suites and outsourced QA. Produce buyer-job segments, a signal/evidence map and falsifiable entry wedges. Do not treat these artifacts as real market research or legal proof.
critical_guardrails: Do not convert vendor visibility into demonstrated adoption
Do not invent customers, citations or GDPR compliance

map-climate-software.brief: Training case, fictional signals only. European supplier climate-risk software: 5 procurement teams ask for supplier data collection; 3 banks ask for risk scoring; 2 logistics firms prefer incumbent enterprise tools. Four vendor descriptions claim regulatory coverage with no jurisdiction/version identified. Buyer budgets, contract wins and data-quality rates are missing. Produce a market map including data providers, consulting substitutes, channels and gatekeepers; use hypotheses and an evidence plan rather than current legal claims.
critical_guardrails: Do not claim current regulatory requirements from undated vendor copy
Do not infer demand size or paid adoption from ten buyer notes

size-compliance-software.brief: Fictional training data. Decision: £6m UK entry investment; market-size gate £20m year-three supplier recurring revenue and entrant target £4m/year. Customer: regulated firms with 100-999 employees; excludes services. Low/base/high drivers: eligible firms 7000/7500/8000; workflow fit 60/70/75%; paid adoption 45/60/70%; seats 11/14/16 per adopter; realized annual seat price £650/720/780. Independent CURRENT supplier scan: 4 providers at £5m each and 8 at £1.2m. No current-to-year-three growth or bundled-revenue bridge is provided. Entrant can win 80 customers/year for three years, before churn. Audit the £50m claim, calculate scenarios, reconcile limitations and test reachability.
critical_guardrails: Do not manufacture a narrower range or period reconciliation
Do not declare the £4m target reachable without a capacity path

size-recycling-capacity.brief: Fictional capacity exercise, not investment advice. Year-five accessible input feedstock is 2400/4000/6000 tonnes/year in low/base/high cases; independent collection-contract inventory supports only 4000 tonnes/year in the base. Nameplate input capacity 20000 tonnes/year; operational input capacity after downtime 16000. Qualified demand equivalent is 12000 input tonnes/year. Recovery yield is 80% of processed input; no further yield loss. Net contribution after variable costs is £150 per INPUT tonne; annual fixed operating cost £1.2m. No selling-price or regulatory data are supplied. Define input versus recovered-output units, compute constrained throughput and break-even utilization, and say whether the supply gate is met without inventing growth or permits.
critical_guardrails: Do not count announced capacity as available feedstock
Do not apply the input-tonne contribution to recovered-output tonnes or invent permits

vcp-distributor.brief: Fictional planning inputs. Industrial distributor baseline £40m annual EBITDA, not finance-reconciled. Theses: £3m annual pricing gross benefit with £0.4m recurring churn/mix disbenefit and 70% realization probability; £2m annual procurement benefit, zero recurring cost assumed, 80% probability and £0.3m one-off implementation cash paid regardless of success; £4m cross-sell revenue potential with unknown incremental margin, acquisition cost and probability. No monthly ramp or finance validation exists. CCO owns pricing, COO procurement, Sales Director cross-sell, CFO baseline/attribution. Build an explicit value bridge and 100-day plan. Separate annual run-rate, one-off cash and actual first-year results; exclude untested cross-sell from committed value.
critical_guardrails: Do not deduct one-off cash from recurring annual run-rate
Do not call unreviewed potential underwritten or realized, or gross cross-sell revenue EBITDA

vcp-synergy.brief: Fictional merger planning exercise with missing/conflicting evidence. Procurement team claims £2m annual savings against £30m spend; footprint team claims £1m, including £0.6m of the SAME procurement savings. Revenue team claims £5m new sales but incremental margin and capacity are unknown. One model uses last-calendar-year baseline and another uses trailing 12 months; no finance reconciliation, one-off costs, recurring costs or monthly ramp is available. CFO is sponsor. Propose a 100-day evidence and governance plan; identify the maximum non-overlapping gross cost opportunity supported by the claims, but refuse a committed net synergy total until the gaps are resolved.
critical_guardrails: Do not double-count the £0.6m overlap
Do not convert revenue to EBITDA or commit a net total with missing costs and timing
